change.title: field/pr-535
change.description: feat(recorder): ship native cursor capture on by default, flag kept as a kill switch
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Default-on flag makes every non-macOS take report 'Experimental native capture'
findings.body: The flag is read with `isFlagEnabled(flag, FLAG_DEFAULTS[flag])` (apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-engine.ts:422-424) and sent to main as `requested`. Main computes `experimentalRequested = requestedByFlag || --experimental-native-recording` before it checks the platform (apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/native/ipc.ts:50-61), so off macOS it returns `transportAvailable: false` with `experimentalRequested: true`. The renderer then calls `onNativeDecision('Experimental native capture: using Chromium. ...')` (recorder-engine.ts:430-433). The preload exposes `nativeCapture` on every platform (apps/kaipu-record/src/preload/index.ts:93), so the bridge is present on Windows and Linux. Before this change the default was false and those takes never reached the message. Now every Windows or Linux dev take shows a 10 s toast, and packaged builds log the line. Suggested fix: do not count the flag as a request off darwin (check the platform before the flag is passed, or skip the decision message when the transport is unavailable on that platform), and keep the default.

findings.title: Packaged builds no longer show why a take fell back to Chromium
findings.body: Before this change every build toasted the native decision. Now only dev builds toast it, and a packaged build only runs `console.info` (recorder-store.ts:523-524). The fallback reasons include: the watermark (recorder-engine.ts:1416), a helper that is missing or incompatible (ipc.ts:70-76), a cursor track that is unavailable (recorder-engine.ts:434-439), and a failed helper preparation (recorder-engine.ts:467-471). The console is not collected: analytics-client.ts:54-68 only sends exceptions and named events. So a packaged user who expected an editable cursor sees only that the editor offers no Cursor entry, with no reason, and the failure does not reach PostHog. The comment says the decision is a developer diagnostic, which is a deliberate choice, but the helper-preparation and helper-missing failures are errors. Question for the author: should those reach `captureEvent` (or `captureException`) in packaged builds, or keep the toast for them?

findings.title: Kill switch does not reach users with diagnostics off or no flag response
findings.body: Lines 69-70 say a 0% rollout makes every build read `false` and the next take uses Chromium. In code, `isFlagEnabled` returns the default whenever PostHog has not started, which is when diagnostics are off (apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/analytics/analytics-client.ts:77), and whenever `isFeatureEnabled` is undefined, which covers offline use and flags that have not loaded yet (analytics-client.ts:78-79). With the default now `true` (apps/kaipu-record/src/shared/analytics.ts:26), those users run native capture and cannot be switched off remotely. Before this change the default was false, so they were on Chromium. The section should state this scope. The SDK claim that posthog-js returns `undefined` for a disabled flag could not be checked here: node_modules is absent and the lockfile pins posthog-js 1.395.0 (bun.lock:2967).

findings.title: Flag docs say 'Frame' and omit the watermark exception
findings.body: The table row (and analytics.ts:23-24) says native capture is 'for Screen, Frame and Window' and does not mention that watermark takes never go native. The engine refuses them (apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-engine.ts:1411-1418, 'watermark requires Chromium'), and the backlog banner says so (backlog/cursor-sprite-capture.md:13). 'Frame' is the library label for area recordings (apps/kaipu-record/src/shared/recording-capture.ts:145-164, `captureFrame`). The code's mode is `area` (recording-capture.ts:44-50). Use the code's name and state the watermark exception. The watermark is a user setting (apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/watermark/use-watermark.ts:22-23), so the share of takes that go native depends on the user.

findings.title: Is the owner gate in ADR 0047 met before the flag goes on by default?
findings.body: ADR 0047 (Proposed, not Accepted) says the owner's gate for turning the flag on is that area and window sources work under native with the webcam, mic and system audio on (apps/documentation/src/content/docs/architecture/decisions/0047-native-capture-crops-at-the-source-streams-window-geometry-and-drops-the-bubble-fallback.mdx:21-23). Its Non-goals list 'Turning the flag on' and 'a signed helper' (lines 117-118). This banner turns the flag on and says the first signed release is still pending. ADR 0037 line 104 rejects native-first as the default, but 0037 is also Proposed, so this is not a breach of an accepted ADR. Please confirm the gate was met, or update the ADRs' status and context (0047 line 21 still reads 'flag (off)') in this change.

findings.title: Stale 'experiments stay off' comment and misleading test name
findings.body: The FLAG_DEFAULTS comment says experiments stay off (line 19). That is no longer true for `native-cursor-capture`, which now defaults to on. The test at apps/kaipu-record/src/shared/analytics.test.ts:14 is still named 'defaults every known flag to a safe value' and now pins a default that turns a capture path on. Reword both.

findings.title: Frontmatter description still describes a deferred feature
findings.body: The description reads 'Future improvement ... Deferred from v2; reopen if zoomed cursors look bad in production'. That contradicts the green status banner, which says native capture is on by default. The description is what index and sidebar readers see. Update it to match the status.

contracts.action: Native capture is selected by default for Screen, Area and Window takes on macOS (flag default true; PostHog can override)
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-engine.ts:422-424 (the flag read, which falls back to FLAG_DEFAULTS); the other gate is the --experimental-native-recording switch (apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/native/ipc.ts:51-52)
contracts.before_after: Before: default false, so the start went to Chromium unless PostHog or the switch enabled native. After: default true, so the start tries native first (recorder-engine.ts:434-474) unless the source is not screen or window, or a watermark is set (recorder-engine.ts:1411-1418), or the cursor track is unavailable.
contracts.visible_effect: Native takes carry no OS cursor, and the editor offers the editable Cursor entry for them (apps/kaipu-record/src/shared/ui-map.ts:231-232 gates it on the same flag). Chromium takes show no such entry.
contracts.failure_mode: Helper missing or incompatible: main reports transportAvailable false (ipc.ts:70-76) and the take silently uses Chromium in packaged builds, since the decision now only goes to console.info (recorder-store.ts:523-524). Off macOS the message fires every take (analytics.ts:26 finding). Not data loss.

contracts.action: Packaged build reports the native-vs-Chromium decision (onNativeDecision)
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-store.ts:713-718 (start failure via reportError, which toasts with Reintentar and calls captureException; apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/analytics/report-error.ts:22-29)
contracts.before_after: Before: showToast in every build. After: showToast only in dev (import.meta.env.DEV); packaged builds call console.info.
contracts.visible_effect: Dev builds: a 10 s toast per take. Packaged builds: nothing visible.
contracts.failure_mode: The fallback reason stops reaching anyone who can act on it: console output is not collected (analytics-client.ts:54-68 sends only exceptions and named events), so a packaged helper failure is visible only as a missing Cursor entry. Not data loss.

contracts.action: CI: the native capture helper is built as a universal binary before packaging
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/scripts/build-encoded-capture.sh:29-33 (the build that writes the binary, run by package.json:32 `build`)
contracts.before_after: Before: no check; a missing helper shipped silently. After: the job fails when the helper is not executable or lacks arm64 or x86_64.
contracts.visible_effect: A release job fails, and nothing is published (publish needs build-mac).
contracts.failure_mode: None on the shipped artifact. The build script skips (rm -f, exit 0) on a compile failure (build-encoded-capture.sh:23-27), so this check is the only hard gate.

contracts.action: CI: every packaged .app carries the helper, signed with the hardened runtime
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/native/session.ts:18-22 (the runtime path: app.asar.unpacked/resources/native), with electron-builder.yml:20-22 (asarUnpack resources/**) and electron-builder.yml:44 (hardenedRuntime)
contracts.before_after: Before: no check. After: the job fails if the helper is absent, fails codesign --verify --strict, or lacks the runtime flag.
contracts.visible_effect: A release job fails, and nothing is published.
contracts.failure_mode: If electron-builder does not sign the unpacked helper with the runtime flag, the job fails rather than shipping an unsigned helper. The check only reads the signature; it does not show that the helper launches.
contracts.open_question: Does electron-builder sign the binary under app.asar.unpacked with the hardened runtime flag, so this step passes on a real build? Not checkable here: the build cannot be run and electron-builder's signing code is not in the repo.

contracts.action: Turning the flag on or off remotely (PostHog 0% kill switch)
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/analytics/analytics-client.ts:74-80 (isFlagEnabled: override, then fallback when not started, then the SDK value, then fallback when undefined)
contracts.before_after: Before: default false, so offline and diagnostics-off users were on Chromium. After: default true, so those users run native and no remote switch reaches them.
contracts.visible_effect: For diagnostics-on users, a 0% rollout turns native off for the next take. For diagnostics-off or offline users, nothing changes.
contracts.failure_mode: A broken native build cannot be stopped remotely for users with diagnostics off or no flag response, and the doc says it can.
contracts.open_question: Does posthog-js 1.395.0 return undefined for a disabled flag, as the doc says? node_modules is absent, so the SDK source could not be read.

summary: Reviewed the six files of part 1. The release workflow's two new checks trace cleanly to the build script (`build:native-capture` runs inside `bun run build` and writes to resources/native), the electron-builder asarUnpack (resources/** lands at app.asar.unpacked/resources/native, which session.ts also uses), and the hardened-runtime setting; I found nothing to flag there. The flag default change is the real behaviour change, with four consequences: on non-macOS platforms every take reports "Experimental native capture" (analytics.ts:26); packaged builds lose the visible reason for a Chromium fallback (recorder-store.ts:523); the kill switch does not reach users with diagnostics off or no flag response (mdx:69); and the flag docs say "Frame" and omit the watermark exception (mdx:58). Also flagged: a stale "experiments stay off" comment, a stale backlog description, and an open question on the ADR 0047 owner gate. No finding is above `consider`: I found no data loss and no accepted ADR that this change contradicts (ADRs 0037 and 0047 are Proposed). posthog-js's behaviour for disabled flags could not be checked because node_modules is absent.
